page0.text:
The sound was like hitting steel.
"Haah... Haah... Haah... Haah...!"
He arrived there still breathing heavily.
His footsteps are loud and their rhythm is erratic.
Staggering forward, he leaves the door flung wide open. He can hardly stay on his feet, pulled forward only by his falling body.

page1.text:
He looks around.
The church is empty after morning service.
Light is only provided by the sun streaking through the windows above.
The silence creates a solemn air, and the still atmosphere creates a profound stillness.
His very presence is heresy.

page2.text:
"Ah... Haah... Haah...!"
No, that would be wrong.
He did not merely come to this place.
With ragged breath and unfocused eyes...
With shaking limbs that wither and sway...
He desperately fled for shelter.
That is the true answer.
His wretchedness is that of prey fleeing from a predatory hound.

page3.text:
"It has been six days since the war started. You are the first person to come here."
"Ungh...!"
He forces his body upright.
Just when did this man appear?
With bloodshot eyes, he peers at the priest standing at the altar and mutters incoherently.

page4.text:
...
The priest frowns.
He could not fully understand the boy, but assumes he is here to ask for help.
He wants protection.
The Master who lost his Servant may ask for protection under the condition that he withdraws from the war.
That place of refuge, the last sanctuary, is this church.
And the master of this place, Kirei Kotomine, is the priest.

page5.text:
"...So you will withdraw from the war, boy?"
The boy responds to that solemn voice with a sparking flame.
"O-of course! Are you telling me to die...!?
Look, I can't kill anyone without my Servant, so I don't wanna be a Master...! I-I'm a normal person. I'm a victim, right!? It's unfair for anyone to kill someone like me...!"

page6.text:
...
The priest does not answer and only looks at the intruder.
He looks beyond the boy.
As if to peer beneath the skin, bone, and sinew to that which lies beneath.

page7.text:
"...What? You got a problem?"
"I do not have any opinions. You are the first person to withdraw this time, and the first user of this church since it has started. I shall welcome you in the stead of my father, as the overseer of the war."
"Huh? What, so I'm the only one to quit? Fucking hell, what a nightmare. I don't know what my grandfather will say if he hears of it.
Ugh, this is all your guys' fault...! It's so unfair I got a piece of shit like Rider!"

page8.text:
He pounds his fist into the floor in a rage.
The sound echoes like a bell, and the priest smiles with great interest.

page9.text:
"So Rider was useless, then?"
"That's right! ...What the hell, she was only talk.
She died so easily even though I helped her that much. Any other Servant would've been way more useful!"
"..."

page10.text:
"...Yeah. Even then, I still did well. I did just as my grandfather told me, and everything was set!
But they all got in my way...! It was two against one. There was no way I could've won against that.
...That's right, it wasn't my fault that I lost.
It was just the difference in the quality of our Servants. But... they were so smug about it...!!!"

page11.text:
And then he squirms on the ground.
He strikes the floor bitterly, laments his misfortune, and obsesses over his obstacles.
But his resentful voice dissipates quickly.
Hatred of such a level cannot break the silence of this church.

page12.text:
"Damn...damn, damn, damn, damn...!"
He repeats his cries of agony.
In the midst of it...
Footsteps.
The priest's steps echo through the room as if they were shattering the frozen air.

page13.text:
The father slowly puts his hand on the child's shoulder.
"...So.
That means you still have the will to fight?"
He looks down at the loser and says so with a gentle voice.

page14.text:
"Huh...?"
He cannot understand the priest's words.
The clergy in black has a polite smile on his face.
"You are in luck. I happen to have one Servant who is available right now."
The priest offers a new salvation, barely able to restrain a rapturous joy.
